links.outcome: Case-grounded content quality of LLM diagnostic and prescription outputs versus structural completeness
links.effect: Structural completeness 99.3-100.0%, but normalized content scores 40.7%-54.1%; general-purpose models averaged 50.0%, TCM-specific models 41.3%; cross-block logic consistency 60.8%-66.8%.
links.quote: Structural completeness was nearly saturated (99.3-100.0%), but normalized content scores ranged from 40.7% to 54.1%.

unlisted_practices: Component-level evidence-constrained rubric separating content quality from cross-block logic consistency to localize failures
LLM-as-judge with retrieval validated against blinded senior clinician ratings and perturbation stress testing

screen.reason: The study develops and applies a benchmark (TCMClinicalReason-Bench) using electronic health record cases to evaluate clinical reasoning and logic consistency across several LLMs without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
